title: Performance Profiling knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Performance Profiling”?
options: It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Measure a reproducible workload before optimizing, and compare correctness plus CPU, memory, allocation, and target-specific costs.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
questions.answer_key: Measure a reproducible workload before optimizing, and compare correctness plus CPU, memory, allocation, and target-specific costs.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Measure a reproducible workload before optimizing, and compare correctness plus CPU, memory, allocation, and target-specific costs. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Performance Profiling”?
options: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Performance Profiling”?
options: Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements.
questions.answer_key: A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
